name: Arches National Park
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Arches National Park in eastern Utah protects over 2,000 natural stone arches — the densest concentration of such formations in the world — along with pinnacles, balanced rocks, and eroded sandstone fins. The landscape was shaped over 300 million years as salt deposits, sandstone layers, and erosion created the park's distinctive red-rock formations. Originally proclaimed a national monument by President Herbert Hoover in 1929, it was redesignated as a national park in 1971. Delicate Arch, the park's most iconic feature, has become a widely recognized symbol of Utah and appears on the state's license plates.
